LESSON: LANGUAGE USE 11.3.1 ADJECTIVES ONE AND TWO- SYLLABLE ADJECTIVES

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade one
Subject: General
Strand: Strand 11
Topic 11.3: Language Use 11.3.1 Adjectives one and two- syllable adjectives
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Language Use 11.3.1 Adjectives one and two- syllable adjectives, part of Strand 11 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade one General.

Key inquiry question: How do we talk about people, things or places?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. recognise signs of adjectives for effective communication,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Language Use 11.3.1 Adjectives one and two- syllable adjectives in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. state words which describe people, places or things for clarity,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Language Use 11.3.1 Adjectives one and two- syllable adjectives in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. use describing words to talk about people, places and objects, • In small groups or pairs, learners are guided to observe, fingerspell and sign vocabulary related to adjectives. • Individually,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Language Use 11.3.1 Adjectives one and two- syllable adjectives in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

C. use describing words to talk about people, places and objects, • In small groups or pairs, learners are guided to observe, fingerspell and sign vocabulary related to adjectives. • Individually,

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Language Use 11.3.1 Adjectives one and two- syllable adjectives together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Learning to learn: The learner practises self-discipline as they sign about objects in a picture/photograph/video clip by using correct adjectives.

Values:
Unity: developed as the learner shows team spirit during language games.

Link to

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Life skills: self-esteem is enhanced as learners describe objects using adjectives correctly.

Links to other Learning Areas:
Adjectives are learnt in Kiswahili and Kenyan Sign Language.
